note: BUG#22 (QualityControl ledger) — a route (to:) given to a creates: command whose plan is NOT complete_state (Governance::RoleTransition.Grant — legacy_implicit_creation?'s domain) forces CommandInterpreter#hydrate_existing's own find-or-NotFound, ignoring the command's own facts-derived identity entirely, regardless of creates?. Unmodified Rust's generated dispatch decided create-vs-find purely from the command's static creates: flag, so it never read the route at all — it minted a fresh RoleTransition from the real facts (from_role/to_role/starts_at) and silently succeeded where Ruby correctly refuses NotFound ("no RoleTransition with from_role.value, to_role.value, starts_at.value \"nonexistent-route-target\""). Confirmed genuinely broken before this fixture existed. Originally found via Hecks::Fuzzing::SequenceGenerator.generate("examples/pizzas", seed: 3, steps: 25, adversarial: 0.3) step 18's own routing_key adversarial mutation (a scalar to: alongside real flat facts, no with: key).
